title: Associations between empathy dimensions, love language expression, and relationship satisfaction among university students in Northern Cyprus.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to explore relationships among aspects of empathy, love language expression, and relationship satisfaction among university students. We also examined attachment styles as a theoretical framework; however, severe measurement limitations prevented valid inferences about attachment patterns.
METHOD: We used a cross-sectional study of 513 students in Northern Cyprus (M = 20.99 years; 56.3% female) using the Relationship Scales Questionnaire (RSQ), Five Love Languages Scale (FLLS), Basic Empathy Scale (BES), and Relationship Assessment Scale (RAS). We used snowball sampling with power analysis showing adequate power to detect medium effects. However, we found important limitations in the measurement: the RSQ showed unacceptably low reliability (α = 0.27 to 0.61), and attachment measures are therefore uninterpretable.
RESULTS: After revising initial errors in scoring, we found that expression of love language frequency was positively correlated with relationship satisfaction (r = .45), with Quality Time (r = .48) and Gift-Giving (r = .45) being the strongest associations. Cognitive empathy (r = .39) was significantly more highly related to satisfaction than affective empathy (r = .15). Due to the extremely low reliability of the RSQ (0.27-0.61; α), we cannot make any inferences regarding attachment patterns. Gender differences had a small to medium effect, with females displaying greater empathy and increased use of some love languages.
CONCLUSION: The expression of love language and cognitive empathy are positively related to relationship satisfaction in this sample of university students. However, severe measurement restrictions using the attachment scale preclude any conclusions about attachment patterns. Upcoming research should use psychometrically sound measures, such as the Experiences in Close Relationships-Revised (ECR-R) scale.
